There has always been an interest in gen: The word ‘genius’, from the Latin gens (= family) and the term ‘genius’, meaning ‘begetter’, comes from the early Roman cult of a divinity as the head of the family.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: genius一词源自意为“家族”的拉丁语gens和意为“生育者”的genius，其渊源可追溯到早期罗马人把一位神灵奉为家族之主的信仰。
column13: head of the family|家族之主

There has always been an interest in gen: In its earliest form, genius was concerned with the ability of the head of the family, the paterfamilias, to perpetuate himself.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 这个词最早指的是一家之主，也就是家父，繁衍后代、延续自身血脉的能力。
prodigies|n. 神童: head of the family|一家之主
column7: paterfamilias|n. 古罗马的男性家长

There has always been an interest in gen: Gradually, genius came to represent a person’s characteristics and thence an individual’s highest attributes derived from his ‘genius’ or guiding spirit.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 后来，这个词逐渐用来指一个人的特质，进而指一个人从自己的守护神那里获得的最高禀赋。

There has always been an interest in gen: Today, people still look to stars or genes, astrology or genetics, in the hope of finding the source of exceptional abilities or personal characteristics.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 直到今天，人们仍寄望于星辰或基因，求诸占星术或遗传学，希望找到非凡才能或个人特质的来源。

There has always been an interest in gen: The concept of genius and of gifts has become part of our folk culture, and attitudes are ambivalent towards them.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: “天才”和“天赋”这两个概念已成为民间文化的一部分，人们对它们却怀有矛盾的心情。

There has always been an interest in gen: We envy the gifted and mistrust them.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 我们既羡慕有天赋的人，又不信任他们。

There has always been an interest in gen: In the mythology of giftedness, it is popularly believed that if people are talented in one area, they must be defective in another, that intellectuals are impractical, that prodigies burn too brightly too soon and burn out, that gifted people are eccentric, that they are physical weaklings, that there’s a thin line between genius and madness, that genius runs in families, that the gifted are so clever they don’t need special help, that giftedness is the same as having a high IQ, that some races are more intelligent or musical or mathematical than others, that genius goes unrecognised and unrewarded, that adversity makes men wise or that people with gifts have a responsibility to use them.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 围绕天赋流传着种种迷思。人们普遍相信，一个人若在某一方面有天赋，在另一方面就一定有缺陷，知识分子也都不切实际。还有说法认为，神童过早大放异彩，才华也会早早耗尽。有天赋的人性情古怪、身体孱弱，天才与疯狂只有一线之隔，天才会在家族中代代相传，有天赋的人聪明到无需特别帮助。还有一种看法把天赋等同于高智商，认为某些族群比其他族群更聪明，或更有音乐、数学天赋。类似的说法还有，天才得不到赏识和回报，逆境使人明智，或者有天赋的人有责任运用自己的天赋。
column11: burn too brightly too soon|过早大放异彩
column15: a thin line between|两者间细微的界限
column18: runs in families|在家族中代代相传
column29: have a responsibility to|有责任做……

There has always been an interest in gen: Language has been enriched with such terms as ‘highbrow’, ‘egghead’, ‘blue-stocking’, ‘wiseacre’, ‘know-all’, ‘boffin’ and, for many, ‘intellectual’ is a term of denigration.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 语言里也多了许多这样的称呼，如“高雅人士”“书呆子”“才女”“自作聪明的人”“万事通”和“科研怪才”；在许多人眼中，连“知识分子”都是个贬称。
prodigies|n. 神童: egghead|n. 书呆子；知识分子的戏称
column7: blue-stocking|n. 对有学问女性的旧称
column9: know-all|n. 自以为什么都懂的人

There has always been an interest in gen: The nineteenth century saw considerable interest in the nature of genius, and produced not a few studies of famous prodigies.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 19世纪的人们对天才的本质兴趣浓厚，关于著名神童的研究也为数不少。

There has always been an interest in gen: Perhaps for us today, two of the most significant aspects of most of these studies of genius are the frequency with which early encouragement and teaching by parents and tutors had beneficial effects on the intellectual, artistic or musical development of the children but caused great difficulties of adjustment later in their lives, and the frequency with which abilities went unrecognised by teachers and schools.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 对今天的我们来说，这些关于天才的研究大多有两点尤其值得注意。其一，父母和家庭教师早年的鼓励和教导常常有益于孩子的智力、艺术或音乐才能的发展，却也常使他们在日后的生活中很难适应。其二，老师和学校也常常察觉不到孩子的才能。
geniuses|n. 天才: studies of genius|关于天才的研究
column13: later in their lives|在他们日后的生活中

There has always been an interest in gen: However, the difficulty with the evidence produced by these studies, fascinating as they are in collecting together anecdotes and apparent similarities and exceptions, is that they are not what we would today call norm-referenced.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 不过，这些研究提供的证据有个问题。它们汇集了轶事，以及看似相似的情形和例外，读来虽引人入胜，却没有采用今天所说的“以常模为参照”的方法。

There has always been an interest in gen: In other words, when, for instance, information is collated about early illnesses, methods of upbringing, schooling, etc., we must also take into account information from other historical sources about how common or exceptional these were at the time.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 换句话说，比如在汇集有关童年时所患疾病、养育方式和受教育情况等资料时，我们还必须参考其他史料，看看这些情况在当时有多普遍或多罕见。

There has always been an interest in gen: For instance, infant mortality was high and life expectancy much shorter than today, home tutoring was common in the families of the nobility and wealthy, bullying and corporal punishment were common at the best independent schools and, for the most part, the cases studied were members of the privileged classes.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 例如，当时婴儿死亡率很高，人们的预期寿命也比今天短得多，贵族和富裕家庭请家庭教师十分常见；最好的私立学校里，欺凌和体罚也很普遍，而研究所涉及的人，大多来自特权阶层。

There has always been an interest in gen: It was only with the growth of paediatrics and psychology in the twentieth century that studies could be carried out on a more objective, if still not always very scientific, basis.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 直到20世纪，随着儿科学和心理学的发展，这些研究才得以在更客观的基础上进行，尽管它们仍不总是十分科学。

There has always been an interest in gen: Geniuses, however they are defined, are but the peaks which stand out through the mist of history and are visible to the particular observer from his or her particular vantage point.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 不论怎样界定天才，他们都只是穿过历史迷雾而显现的山峰；某位观察者站在自己的位置上，望见的就是这些山峰。

There has always been an interest in gen: Change the observers and the vantage points, clear away some of the mist, and a different lot of peaks appear.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 换一批观察者，换个观察位置，再拨开一些迷雾，显现出来的就会是另一组山峰。

There has always been an interest in gen: Genius is a term we apply to those whom we recognise for their outstanding achievements and who stand near the end of the continuum of human abilities which reaches back through the mundane and mediocre to the incapable.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 我们把那些成就卓著、因而受到认可的人称为“天才”。他们接近人类能力连续谱的一端；从这一端往回看，依次是普普通通的人、资质平庸的人，直至缺乏能力的人。

There has always been an interest in gen: There is still much truth in Dr Samuel Johnson’s observation, ‘The true genius is a mind of large general powers, accidentally determined to some particular direction’.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 塞缪尔·约翰逊博士的一句话至今仍很有道理：“真正的天才具有强大的通才之能，只是偶然被引向了某个特定的方向。”

There has always been an interest in gen: We may disagree with the ‘general’, for we doubt if all musicians of genius could have become scientists of genius or vice versa, but there is no doubting the accidental determination which nurtured or triggered their gifts into those channels into which they have poured their powers so successfully.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 我们也许不同意“通才”这一说法，因为我们怀疑是否每位天才音乐家当初都能成为天才科学家，反过来也一样。但有一点毋庸置疑：是某些偶然因素培育或激发了他们的天赋，并为之定下方向；他们把才智倾注其中，取得了成功。

There has always been an interest in gen: Along the continuum of abilities are hundreds of thousands of gifted men and women, boys and girls.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 在人类能力的这条连续谱上，有数以十万计的男女老少都颇具天赋。
interest in|对……的兴趣: hundreds of thousands of|数以十万计的

There has always been an interest in gen: What we appreciate, enjoy or marvel at in the works of genius or the achievements of prodigies are the manifestations of skills or abilities which are similar to, but so much superior to, our own.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 在天才的作品或神童的成就中，我们所欣赏、喜爱或惊叹的，是他们所展现出的技能和才干。这些本领与我们的相似，水平却高出许多。

There has always been an interest in gen: But that their minds are not different from our own is demonstrated by the fact that the hard-won discoveries of scientists like Kepler or Einstein become the commonplace knowledge of schoolchildren and the once outrageous shapes and colours of an artist like Paul Klee so soon appear on the fabrics we wear.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 但他们的头脑与我们的并无本质区别，这从以下事实可以看出。开普勒、爱因斯坦这类科学家来之不易的发现，成了学童熟知的常识；像保罗·克利这样的画家笔下那些曾被视为离经叛道的形状和色彩，也很快出现在我们的衣料上。

There has always been an interest in gen: This does not minimise the supremacy of their achievements, which outstrip our own as the sub-four-minute milers outstrip our jogging.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 这丝毫无损于他们成就的卓越。他们的成就远胜于我们的，就像能在四分钟内跑完一英里的选手远远超过慢跑的我们一样。
column7: sub-four-minute|adj. 用时不到四分钟的

There has always been an interest in gen: To think of geniuses and the gifted as having uniquely different brains is only reasonable if we accept that each human brain is uniquely different.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 只有承认每个人的大脑都独一无二，把天才和有天赋的人的大脑也看作独具特点，才说得通。

There has always been an interest in gen: The purpose of instruction is to make us even more different from one another, and in the process of being educated we can learn from the achievements of those more gifted than ourselves.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 教育的目的在于让我们彼此之间更有差异；在受教育的过程中，我们可以向比自己更有天赋的人学习，借鉴他们的成就。
column7: in the process of|在……过程中

There has always been an interest in gen: But before we try to emulate geniuses or encourage our children to do so we should note that some of the things we learn from them may prove unpalatable.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 不过，在试图效仿天才或鼓励孩子这么做之前，我们应当留意，从他们身上学到的有些东西或许并不好接受。

There has always been an interest in gen: We may envy their achievements and fame, but we should also recognise the price they may have paid in terms of perseverance, single-mindedness, dedication, restrictions on their personal lives, the demands upon their energies and time, and how often they had to display great courage to preserve their integrity or to make their way to the top.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 我们也许羡慕他们的成就与声名，但也应看到他们可能付出的代价，包括持之以恒、心无旁骛、全身心投入，个人生活受到限制，精力和时间被大量占用。也应看到，为了坚守操守或登上事业顶峰，他们往往得拿出极大的勇气。
column17: make their way to the top|登上事业顶峰

There has always been an interest in gen: Genius and giftedness are relative descriptive terms of no real substance.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: “天才”和“天赋”是相对的描述性用语，本身并没有实质内容。

There has always been an interest in gen: We may, at best, give them some precision by defining them and placing them in a context but, whatever we do, we should never delude ourselves into believing that gifted children or geniuses are different from the rest of humanity, save in the degree to which they have developed the performance of their abilities.
人们一直对天才和神童感兴趣。: 给这些用语下定义，并把它们放在具体语境中，我们最多也只能让它们稍微精确一些。但无论怎样，都不应自欺地认为有天赋的孩子或天才与其他人有别，唯一的差别在于，他们把自身能力发挥到了什么程度。
column9: delude ourselves into believing|自欺地相信
column14: performance of their abilities|能力的发挥
